A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ε-VAE research, with matching methods and identifiable retained experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet reconstruction, unconditional generation, and ablation results in Tables 1–3 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original ImageNet and COCO reconstruction, class-conditional generation, and supplementary experiments, while retaining the earlier empirical results.

M1.justification: The conditional diffusion decoder, latent concatenation, velocity prediction, perceptual and trajectory-matching losses, and noise/time schedules remain unchanged. ε-VAE-SD introduces an experimental encoder configuration, without establishing a new proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ImageNet reconstruction and unconditional generation. v2 adds COCO-2017 reconstruction and class-conditional ImageNet generation (Tables 2–3). The original unconditional tasks remain in Appendix D; higher-resolution reconstruction was already covered in v1.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained controlled VAE comparisons, v2 evaluates VQGAN, LlamaGen, SD-VAE, SDXL-VAE, and LiteVAE in reconstruction comparisons, and Asym-VAE and Omni-VAE in generation comparisons. Appendix D also adds a plain diffusion ADM comparator. Newly discussed diffusion autoencoders are not automatically counted as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce the 34M-parameter SD encoder configuration, target-resolution fine-tuning, PSNR/SSIM, full ImageNet 50K and COCO 5K reconstruction evaluation, and H100 generation-throughput measurements. These extend the protocol substantially. The PDFs do not establish that v1's retained 10K-image evaluations were rerun using the new sample counts.

E4.justification: v2 adds a plain ADM control, examines the benefit of higher-resolution fine-tuning, and supplies SD-VAE case studies emphasizing faces and text. v1's extended decoder-scale, compression, and seed galleries are removed, but the original quantitative ablations and main compression/seed examples remain. These are focused changes to an otherwise retained analysis suite.

E5.justification: Both versions show qualitative variation across reconstruction seeds, without quantitative repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Removing additional example images does not change the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial new results appear in v2 Tables 1–3. At 8× downsampling, Table 2 reports ImageNet rFID 0.47 for ε-VAE-SD(M) versus 0.74 for SD-VAE; Table 3 reports class-conditional FID 9.39 versus 11.63. These are added comparisons under new configurations. v1 Tables 1–3 and 5 retain their numerical results as v2 Tables 7, 8, 4, and 6. The original V100 decoder timings are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–13 are substantively retained. Notation corrections and the new verbal interpretation of conditional posterior approximation do not introduce a theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v2 reframes novelty around a practical diffusion autoencoder and makes computational efficiency a central contribution. Its abstract and introduction add explicit claims of 22% better generation quality and 2.3× inference throughput, alongside stronger positioning against existing autoencoders. The throughput claim depends on increased compression; the basic denoising-as-decoding claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 explains how shorter latent sequences accelerate generation, interprets the added ADM comparison through conditional posterior approximation, and notes a quality cost from omitting the downstream variational-bound loss. The original discussion of stochasticity, perceptual fidelity, resolution generalization, and memory limitations is retained in Appendix A.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies encoder parameter counts, omission of the downstream DiT variational-bound loss, and H100 timing hardware. Existing optimizer, loss-weight, augmentation, and JAX/TPU details are largely relocated. v1's 10,000-image evaluation disclosure and V100 timing details disappear. The loss disclosure alone does not establish a change to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: A substantial new diffusion-decoder discussion covers DiffusionAE, DiVAE, Würstchen, distillation/consistency approaches, and DiTo, with explicit distinctions concerning objectives, sampling efficiency, and resolution generalization. The introduction now acknowledges prior diffusion autoencoding and repositions the contribution around practical joint design. Several generic language-model and tokenization references are removed.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: discussion moves to Appendix A, original scaling and unconditional-generation evaluations move to Appendix D, and standard-configuration comparisons become central. The introduction and generation section are rewritten, ε-VAE-lite/SD terminology is introduced, and visualization and impact-statement sections are added.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to double-column layout, adds three benchmark tables and two SD-VAE comparison figures, and relocates and reformats retained displays. v1 Figures 4–5 become v2 Figures 5–6, while v1's three extended appendix galleries are removed. Table highlighting, captions, sizing, and placement change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's reliance on a lightweight encoder configuration and controlled generic-VAE comparisons. Standard SD configurations, modern baselines, COCO evaluation, distortion metrics, and class-conditional quality/throughput comparisons strengthen practical validation (Tables 1–3), while original controlled results remain available. Expanded related work also clarifies the contribution. Removed decoder-only timings and incomplete fine-tuning details limit transparency, but the broader, more relevant evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
